info.title: Social Poster internal API
info.description: Cross-platform publishing API. Two auth modes share every /v1 route (D-023): app mode uses a client-credentials JWT, user mode uses the signed-in user’s Supabase session JWT and acts as the first-party poster-web app.

servers.description: The service root; deployments front this with TLS.

bearerAuth.description: App mode: the token from POST /v1/oauth/token. User mode: a Supabase session JWT.

access_token.description: JWT whose sub is the app id.

mode.description: Which auth mode the caller used.

AuthContext.description: Who the API thinks you are. Identical shape in both auth modes.

unit.description: How the platform counts length. utf16_code_units is what TikTok calls "runes"; utf8_bytes is a byte budget (YouTube descriptions); characters counts code points.

forbidden_characters.description: Characters the platform rejects outright, e.g. < and > on YouTube.

ErrorEnvelope.description: The single error envelope used by every non-2xx response.

post.summary: Exchange client credentials for a short-lived app token
post.description: Form-encoded, per OAuth2. The returned JWT is valid for 15 minutes and its sub claim identifies the app. App credentials alone never authorize publishing: acting for a user also requires that user’s grant.

401.description: Unknown client_id, wrong client_secret, or disabled app.

429.description: Too many token requests; honor Retry-After.

get.summary: Report who the API thinks you are
get.description: Returns the acting app and user for the presented token. The response shape is identical in both auth modes, which makes it the cheapest way for a client to confirm its credentials and the user it is acting for.

parameters.name: user_id
parameters.description: The user to act as. Required in app mode for user-scoped work; in user mode it must equal the token subject or the request is rejected with forbidden_user.

403.description: User-mode token does not match the requested user_id.

429.description: Per-app rate limit exceeded; honor Retry-After.

get.description: Every limit the constraint engine enforces, so no client hard-codes a platform rule (CLAUDE.md rule 9). Each spec carries its own `sources` and a `provisional` flag: while provisional, the numbers come from platform documentation rather than the aggregator actually used to post, which is often stricter. Limits marked `max_duration_is_per_account` are an optimistic ceiling that only the platform can confirm for a given account.

429.description: Per-app rate limit exceeded; honor Retry-After.

post.summary: Check a post against platform rules without creating it
post.description: Runs exactly the validation POST /v1/posts runs, and returns exactly the same 422 envelope, so a composer can show per-platform warnings before submitting rather than reimplementing the rules. Nothing is created and nothing is reserved. A clean post returns 200; any violation returns 422 with one `details` entry per failing target.

403.description: User-mode token does not match the requested user_id.

404.description: A connection or media id does not exist for this user.

422.description: One or more targets failed platform rules; see details.

429.description: Per-app rate limit exceeded; honor Retry-After.

post.summary: Upload media, or get a signed URL to upload it directly
post.description: Two paths, chosen by Content-Type. `multipart/form-data` sends the bytes through the API, which stores and probes them and returns a ready media row; it is capped in size. `application/json` returns a signed upload URL instead, for large video that should not pass through the API process — PUT the bytes to that URL and then call /complete. Media is uploaded once and referenced by id from any number of posts (FR-07).

202.description: Signed URL issued; nothing is usable until /complete.

400.description: Malformed request, unsupported type, or file too large.

403.description: User-mode token does not match the requested user_id.

429.description: Per-app rate limit exceeded; honor Retry-After.

post.description: Probes the uploaded object for duration and dimensions and marks the media ready. Until this succeeds the media cannot be posted, and referencing it yields the `media_not_ready` constraint code.

400.description: The object is missing or could not be probed.

404.description: No such media for this user.

post.summary: Submit a post to one or more connected accounts
post.description: Validates every target and creates all of them or none (§5). Send an `Idempotency-Key` header: the same key with the same body returns the original result, and the same key with a different body is 409 `idempotency_conflict`. Keys are scoped per app and kept at least 24 hours. Omitting `schedule_at` means dispatch as soon as the post is ready.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Strongly recommended. Without it a retry creates a second post.

403.description: forbidden_user, or grant_missing for a connection.

404.description: A connection or media id does not exist for this user.

409.description: Same Idempotency-Key with a different body.

422.description: One or more targets failed platform rules; see details.

429.description: Per-app rate limit exceeded; honor Retry-After.

get.summary: Read a post and its targets

200.description: The post, with per-target state and outcomes.

404.description: No such post for this app and user.

patch.description: Re-validates constraints (FR-13). Refused with 409 `too_late` once any target has begun dispatching, because the content may already be on its way.

403.description: forbidden_user, or grant_missing for a connection.

404.description: No such post, connection, or media for this user.

422.description: The edit fails platform rules; see details.

post.description: Cancels every target that has not begun dispatching (§6). Returns 409 `too_late` when nothing could be canceled. A post already canceled returns 200 with an empty `canceled_target_ids`, so a retry is safe.

404.description: No such post for this app and user.

409.description: Every target had already begun dispatching or finished.
